title: Make water safe with bleach
summary: EPA drops per gallon for 6% and 8.25% bleach, plus cloudy water, wait time and the smell test.

sources.title: EPA: Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water
CDC: How to Make Water Safe in an Emergency

blocks.text: Use **only plain, unscented chlorine bleach** that says it is suitable for disinfection. **No** scented bleach, color-safe bleach, splash-less bleach, or bleach with added cleaners. Check the label for **6%** or **8.25%** sodium hypochlorite.

blocks.alt: Bleach drops per 1 gallon of water: 8 drops of 6 percent bleach, or 6 drops of 8.25 percent bleach. For cloudy, colored or very cold water, double the drops. Stir, then wait 30 minutes. It should smell slightly of chlorine. If it does not, add the dose again and wait 15 more minutes. Use plain, unscented bleach only.
blocks.caption: Bleach drops per gallon, from the EPA table above.

items: Pour the water through a clean cloth, paper towel or coffee filter if it is cloudy. Let particles settle first.
Use a clean dropper and **fresh** bleach (kept at room temperature for less than one year).
Add the dose from the table.
**Cloudy, colored or very cold water: double the dose.**
Stir. Let it stand for **30 minutes**.
**Smell test:** it should smell slightly of chlorine. If it doesn't, add the dose again and wait **15 more minutes**. If it still has no chlorine smell, don't drink it. Find another source.

blocks.text: If the chlorine taste is too strong, pour the water between two clean containers and let it stand a few hours.
If your bleach is a different strength

The EPA table covers only 6% and 8.25%. CDC publishes one dose for any strength from 5% to 9%: **2 drops per quart, 8 drops per gallon, 40 drops (1/2 teaspoon) per 5 gallons**. Double it for cloudy, colored or very cold water, and wait at least 30 minutes.

items: It kills germs. It does **not** remove fuel, toxic chemicals or radioactive material. Water that may have those can't be made safe this way.
It does not kill every parasite. Chlorine tablets don't kill Cryptosporidium. Chlorine dioxide tablets do.
If a flooded private well is your source, disinfect and test it afterward, and contact your health department.
